paths.description: Search landing page and primary input; tested desktop, 360x800, light/dark/high-contrast, reduced motion, keyboard/control semantics, performance, network, privacy and memory.
Primary journey from query input to results; selected because results are the core product archetype. Bot verification prevented reaching actual result cards.
Settings/control-heavy archetype covering language, region, theme, privacy toggles, native controls, and app metadata.
Representative HTTP failure and recovery state.

findings.summary: The page omits a viewport meta tag, so mobile Chrome lays it out at 980 CSS pixels and scales the entire interface down.
findings.evidence: Both 360x800 layout captures report hasViewportMeta=false, clientWidth=980 and visualViewport scale=0.367; the mobile screenshots show a miniature desktop interface.
findings.suggestedFix: Add <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"> and verify fluid layout and readable target sizing at narrow widths.

findings.summary: The private-usage-metrics notice uses low-contrast body text.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measures #909093 on #39393b at 3.61:1 for 13px text, below the WCAG 4.5:1 minimum.
findings.suggestedFix: Raise the notice text color contrast to at least 4.5:1 in every theme and recheck the link and close-button states.

findings.summary: A metrics notice occupies the full bottom edge on every fresh load and competes with the primary search task.
findings.evidence: Desktop, light, dark, mobile, results, and settings screenshots all show the persistent notice before interaction. It is dismissible, but it repeatedly consumes prominent viewport space.
findings.suggestedFix: Persist dismissal/choice, reduce the notice to non-blocking inline disclosure, and avoid showing it again after the user has made a choice.

findings.summary: The representative search flow is blocked by a drag-the-slider bot challenge in the audit environment.
findings.evidence: Direct navigation and form submission both reached navigation/bot enforcement; desktop and mobile result captures show “Verifying you’re not a bot” instead of search results.
findings.suggestedFix: Review bot-risk thresholds and provide an accessible, privacy-preserving alternative challenge and clear recovery route for false positives.

findings.summary: Mobile lab loading misses the good LCP threshold despite a fast desktop trace.
findings.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse reports LCP 4.1s and FCP 3.2s (performance 80), while the desktop trace records LCP 1.68s and TBT 0ms. The slower common mobile condition is the divergence.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the mobile critical path, prioritize the logo/search shell, and reduce startup requests so LCP stays at or below 2.5s under mobile throttling.

findings.summary: Transient settings UI is implemented without dialog or popover semantics.
findings.evidence: DOM probes report zero <dialog> and zero [popover] elements on home/settings despite the Quick settings overlay surface; controls are assembled from generic page structures.
findings.suggestedFix: Use popover for transient quick settings or dialog for a modal flow, with declarative light-dismiss, focus management, and Escape behavior.

findings.summary: The homepage has no heading structure.
findings.evidence: The document probe found no h1-h6 elements; main and footer landmarks exist, but the page purpose is represented only by logo/controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a concise visually hidden or visible h1 such as “Brave Search” and keep subsequent page headings hierarchical.

findings.summary: Permissions-Policy is absent despite otherwise strong defensive headers.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive confirms CSP, HSTS, nosniff, SAMEORIGIN, and strict-origin-when-cross-origin, but reports Permissions-Policy missing.
findings.suggestedFix: Send an explicit Permissions-Policy that disables unused powerful features and grants required features only to intended origins.

findings.summary: State and route changes expose no View Transitions integration.
findings.evidence: The CSS/animation probe found no view-transition rules or API evidence; the only animation under reduced motion was a finished zero-duration reveal.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document View Transitions for quick-settings and search state changes, retaining an instant fallback and honoring reduced motion.

findings.summary: No container-query evidence was found for reusable search/settings components.
findings.evidence: The authored CSS exposed by the DOM and the dedicated probe contained no @container or container-type rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable panels/search controls containment and adapt their internal layout with size container queries where they appear in different widths.

findings.summary: The minimal homepage loads a fragmented script-heavy startup payload.
findings.evidence: HAR summary records 72 requests and 516,673 transferred bytes, including 55 scripts (286,474 bytes) and a 128,942-byte stylesheet for a sparse search shell.
findings.suggestedFix: Use coverage/bundle analysis to remove unused homepage modules and CSS, combine only where it reduces overhead, and defer settings/results code until requested.

findings.summary: The app-like search experience advertises a standalone manifest but is not meaningfully installable or offline-capable.
findings.evidence: The fetched manifest has blank name and short_name and no start_url; the settings probe reports no controlling service worker.
findings.suggestedFix: Complete the manifest metadata/start URL and add a service worker with an offline search-shell/failure page, or remove standalone installability signaling if intentionally unsupported.

findings.summary: The public homepage lacks the viewport signal required for mobile-friendly indexing and presentation.
findings.evidence: DOM and both mobile layout captures report no meta viewport and a 980 CSS-pixel layout viewport at scale 0.367.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a standard width=device-width viewport declaration, then verify that crawler/mobile rendering presents readable content without whole-page shrink-to-fit.
